subject: Dedicated capacity proposal: mixed GPU pool, throughput SLAs & commit options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@helios.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal: mixed GPU pool, throughput SLAs & commit options

Hi James —

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is a concise proposal that covers the Dedicated pool options we discussed: three SKU mixes (H100-heavy, A100-balanced, L40S-cost-optimized), expected throughput at the 8k/16k sequence profiles you ran, and two commit structures (12-month reserved vs seasonal burst credits).

Quick highlights:
- Baseline recommendation: A100-balanced pool for steady-state inference (estimated 1.2M tokens/day) with H100 headroom for peak batches.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime + 95th percentile p99.5 token latency SLO (proposal in SLA draft).
- Pricing: we included perf/$ curves and memory tiers; pricing is presented as blended monthly commit with an option to exchange pool mix after 60 days.

Attachments: redwood_offer_v2.xlsx (pricing + SKU mix), throughput_modeling_helios.csv (modeling), sla_draft_helios.pdf (SLA language).

Can you confirm the target commit horizon (12 vs 24 months) and whether Helios needs HSM/KMS integration for key management? I’ll loop in our pricing lead if you want to run alternate discount scenarios.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: James Li <james.li@helios.ai>

Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 13:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal: mixed GPU pool, throughput SLAs & commit options

Ben —

Thanks for sending this over. Overall looks promising. A few clarifying questions from our infra and procurement teams before we escalate:

1) GPU mix: what are the expected perf/$ breakpoints you used to choose A100 as baseline vs L40S? We expect steady traffic but occasional spikes for batch scoring.
2) Memory tiers: some of our models need 80+ GB of GPU memory for fine-tuned variants. Will H100 nodes be required for those workloads?
3) Commitment flexibility: can we shift committed capacity between regions (us-west -> us-east) mid-term if workloads change?
4) Pricing: procurement would like a clear discount schedule for larger commit bands (250k, 500k, 1M token-month equivalents).

Anita (cc) is our procurement lead — she’ll coordinate contract steps.

Best,
James
Head of ML Platforms, Helios AI
james.li@helios.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@helios.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal: mixed GPU pool, throughput SLAs & commit options

James, Anita —

Quick technical answers below. I’ll keep it short and can follow up with a short cost/perf matrix if helpful.

1) Perf/$ breakpoints: the modeling in throughput_modeling_helios.csv uses two axes — token/sec at your avg sequence lengths (8k/16k) and cost-per-inference measured as $/k tokens. L40S gives best perf/$ on small context (<2k tokens) but degrades for large sequence lengths because of memory and kernel fusion limits. For your 8k+ profiles, A100-balanced gives better sustained throughput per dollar; H100 brings ~25–35% latency improvement on multi-token generation and is cost-effective for peak batch windows.

2) Memory: models needing 80+ GB will require H100-80 or equivalent. We can provision a small slice (N nodes) of H100 with larger memory and keep the rest of the pool on A100 to optimize costs. We support heterogenous pools and routing policies so large-model requests pin to the H100 partition.

3) Region flexibility: we support reallocation between regions but cross-region migrations of reserved physical capacity require a 30–45 day notice and may incur a nominal relocation fee (hardware provisioning & network reconfiguration). We can include a one-time region-migration credit in the contract for larger commits.

4) Discount schedule: pricing lead will propose stepped discounts by token-month bands. Priya — can you propose two tiers (250k/500k+) and an aggressive 1M+ corporate discount? Also confirm whether Helios wants credits or percent-off list pricing.

Ben / James — happy to run a short perf test if you want A100 vs H100 samples on your models (20–30 minute run).

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@helios.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal: mixed GPU pool, throughput SLAs & commit options

James / Anita —

Thanks for the clear questions. From a commercial perspective we can structure two clean options:

A) 12-month committed reserve (recommended for predictability)
- Base monthly commit: equivalent to 500k token-month at blended mix (70% A100, 20% H100, 10% L40S)
- Discount: 28% off list at 12-month; ramped discounts for >1M bands (35%+).
- Flex: one pool-mix adjustment allowed after month 2; region migration credit available (one-time).
- SLA: 99.95% uptime; credits tied to monthly availability & p99.5 latency misses.

B) 6-month rolling + burst credits
- Lower base discount (12%); bulk burst credits purchased upfront to cover peak H100 windows.
- Good for seasonal workloads but less favorable perf/$.

If you prefer, we can provide a blended effective $/token table and show the delta vs pure H100 and pure L40S packaging. We can also offer a one-time onboarding credit (two weeks of free burst capacity) on a 12-month commit.

Laura — can you confirm contractual language around region migration fee and SLA credit mechanics?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Anita Gomez <anita.gomez@helios.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@helios.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Draft SLA & region migration clause for Helios (redlines welcome)

Anita / Procurement —

Attached is a short SLA draft reflecting the 99.95% uptime and the p99.5 latency SLO. Key commercial points called out:
- Region migration: customer may request reallocation of reserved capacity between US regions with 30 days' notice; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to fulfill. If re-provisioning requires new hardware provisioning (e.g., different cloud partner region availability), a relocation fee equal to one month's committed spend may apply; we are offering a one-time waiver for the first migration on 12-month commits.
- SLA credits: tiered credit schedule tied to monthly availability and latency misses. Credits apply to next invoice; we can discuss cash credit alternatives.
- Data protection: indicates KMS/HSM integration available, key rotation controls, and audit log delivery cadence.

Please flag any redlines; if this looks workable we can generate an updated pricing workbook and DocuSign envelope.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

[attachment: sla_draft_helios.pdf (application/pdf)]

Team —

Appreciate the detailed responses. Procurement and legal reviewed the SLA draft; the waiver for a single region migration on a 12-month commit is acceptable. We have two asks before we finalize:

1) Can Redwood provide a short perf snapshot on one of our medium models showing A100 vs H100 delta (20–30 minute run)? That will help justify the blended approach to our CFO.
2) Can you move the 12-month commit discount to 30% at the 500k band (we had competing offers at ~29% with less flexible migration terms).

If you can accommodate those two items we are prepared to sign the 12-month reserved commit (DEAL-HELIOS-2027-07) and run a 30-day onboarding window. Please send the DocuSign link when ready.

Thanks,
Anita Gomez
Head of Procurement, Helios AI
procurement@helios.ai
